svg.title: Grouped midpoint moments and straight-line median interpolation use different approximations
svg.desc: Twenty heights in centimetres are grouped into ten to below twenty, twenty to below thirty, and thirty to below fifty, with frequencies six, ten and four. Midpoints fifteen, twenty-five and forty give weighted sum five hundred and squared-midpoint weighted sum fourteen thousand. The midpoint mean estimate is twenty-five centimetres, population variance estimate seventy-five square centimetres and standard deviation estimate five square root three centimetres. The cumulative graph starts at ten centimetres with count zero and passes through twenty six, thirty sixteen and fifty twenty. Median interpolation uses cumulative level ten in the middle class, giving twenty plus four tenths of width ten, equal to twenty-four centimetres under uniform spread within that class. The exact median of twenty raw records would instead average the values at ordered positions ten and eleven, which the grouped table does not supply.
